title: customer-escalation-war-room-lambda-finance-2026-03-12
content:
War-room notes (scratchpad) - Lambda Finance P1 - 2026-03-12

Attendees: Aisha Patel (CS), Carlos Mendoza (SRE), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Ben Liu (Serving Runtime), Marta Gomez (Account Exec)
Slack channel: #escalations-lambda (pin: incident checklist)
Primary contacts at customer: Jo Park (Eng Manager), Ravi Shah (SRE)

Severity: P1 - production outage for ~30% of requests to /generate on dedicated cluster (us-west-2)
Impact window: First reports 2026-03-12 08:14 PDT, spike ended ~09:00 PDT after mitigation, but errors reappeared 09:35-09:48 PDT (brief)
Current status: Stabilized behind fallback (smaller model); still monitoring. Customer is on call and being updated every 15m.

Symptoms observed:
- 500 errors returned from Redwood edge for some routed requests (trace ids in Slack)
- Latency spikes to 8-12s for generation; baseline ~400-600ms
- Error pattern appears correlated with requests hitting model: redwood-large-1 quantized variant on dedicated pool X
- Errors include: KV cache OOM in runtime logs, RPC timeouts between node A and B, and a few segfaults on node B (core dump captured)

Immediate mitigation taken (timeline):
- 08:20 PDT: Rotated traffic to fallback model redwood-medium-1 for affected routes (Priya) -> immediate drop in error rate
- 08:28 PDT: Drained node B from pool X and flagged for investigation (Carlos)
- 08:36 PDT: Increased autoscaler headroom for Dedicated pool X (Ben)
- 09:05 PDT: Customer notified of temporary fallback and ETA for root cause follow-up (Marta)
- 09:35 PDT: Brief recurrence observed; scaled up additional small instances and enabled aggressive prefix caching (Aisha/Priya) -> stabilized at 09:48

Hypotheses (to validate):
1) Regression in recent runtime commit (serving-runtime) that changes KV cache eviction/locking behavior; reproduces under certain sequence lengths and batching patterns. (Hypothesis lead: Ben)
2) Memory leak in quantized execution path for redwood-large-1 variant causing OOM and subsequent segfaults on long-lived processes. (Hypothesis lead: Carlos)
3) Routing/fanout edge bug causing a subset of requests to be routed in a way that overwhelms node B due to imbalanced batching. (Hypothesis lead: Priya)

Data to gather / immediate next checks:
- Collect core dump + runtime log from node B (Carlos) -> location: s3://redwood-incidents/lambda-2026-03-12/nodeB-core.tgz (confirm upload)
- Extract last 1k lines from runtime logs + GC/memory stats for pool X (Ben)
- Check model binary/weights checksum used by pool X vs fallback (Priya)
- Look at request distribution and batching histogram for 07:50-09:50 PDT (Aisha)
- Confirm no infra maintenance or noisy neighbor events in us-west-2 at that time (SRE infra)

Decisions / short-term plan:
- Keep traffic on fallback redwood-medium-1 for customer routes until RCA completed (owner: Marta)
- Recreate a small isolated pool with same config as pool X but with debug symbols and increased logging enabled to reproduce (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-13T12:00Z)
- Run the failing request pattern from captured traces against debug pool to trigger failure locally (owner: Ben, due: 2026-03-13T18:00Z)
- Hold for change freeze on serving-runtime until regression hypothesis validated or ruled out (owner: Aisha, note: communicate to engineering on-call)

Action items (owner - due - status notes):
- Carlos Mendoza - 2026-03-12T14:00Z - upload + sanitize core dump, mark suspicious symbols (in progress)
- Ben Liu - 2026-03-13T18:00Z - reproduce on debug pool + attach gdb trace if segfault (todo)
- Priya Singh - 2026-03-13T12:00Z - repro pool with debug logging + config dump (todo)
- Aisha Patel - 2026-03-12T10:00Z - send 15m incident update to customer and GTM (done)
- Marta Gomez - 2026-03-12T11:00Z - confirm customer comfortable with fallback and ask for permission for extended debugging window (done)
- Engineering On-call (rotation) - 2026-03-12T12:00Z - freeze non-critical deploys for serving-runtime (todo)
- CS Support - 2026-03-12T12:30Z - draft external incident summary for customer postmortem (todo)

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Need to confirm whether redwood-large-1 quantized build on pool X was patched 2026-03-10 (possible regression). Check GitHub PRs against serving-runtime between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-11. (Aisha)
- Might be related to a new autoscaler policy that allows more long-lived processes per node; check autoscaler change logs. (Priya)
- If reproduces locally, capture heap profile (tcmalloc/heap-prof) and kv-cache metrics. (Ben)
- Consider short-term config to reduce sequence length limit for redwood-large-1 on Dedicated pools as mitigation if memory pressure confirmed. (Carlos)

Communication cadence:
- 15m updates until stabilised, then 30m cadence for next 6 hours.
- Internal postmortem channel: Confluence page (linked above) - draft will include timeline, root cause, and preventive actions.

Draft customer-facing summary (to edit) - do not send without CS review:
"We experienced a routing/memory issue affecting a subset of requests to your dedicated cluster in us-west-2 on 2026-03-12. We rotated traffic to a verified fallback model and scaled capacity to mitigate immediate impact. Our engineering team is actively investigating root cause and will share a detailed timeline and long-term fix plan within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption - we recognize this impacted your service and are treating it as highest priority.

Next sync: 2026-03-12 10:30 PDT (call) - agenda: RCA progress, logs review, customer questions

Notes end.

---
Personal scratch: keep meeting light, note customer tone - Jo Park worried about SLA credits; escalate to legal if they push for credits before RCA complete. Also track impact numbers (errors/min, >95th latency) to quantify SLA breach window.
